chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far narrated to me from his father, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Khālid, from 'Abdillah ibn Hammad Al-Basri, from 'Abdillah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman Al-Asam, who said:

Hisham ibn Salim from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) that a man came to him and asked him, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, is your father visited?' He said, 'Yes, and prayer is established next to him,' and he said, 'And prayer is established behind him, and one does not go forward (in front of him).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing prayer at the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) clarifies the specific etiquette of prayer at the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.), emphasizing that while visiting and praying near the grave are permissible, one must avoid standing directly in front of it. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of distinguishing between reverence for the grave and the direction of prayer, ensuring that the Imam’s resting place is honored without being treated as a qibla or an object of prostration itself.
